ABOUT FINNY

FINNY is a growth platform for financial advisors. We are on a mission to make great financial advice easier to find. Today, access to quality financial guidance is limited, not because advisors don't exist, but because the right connections are hard to make when it matters. We're fixing that with AI-powered tools that help advisors find, engage, and retain the clients they can genuinely help.

 

We've raised a $4.5M Seed from Y-Combinator in S24 and now $17M Series A led by Venrock. We work with over 1,000 firms across the wealth management ecosystem, and have been recognized as the leader in fintech innovation—winning #1 at the Morningstar Fintech Showcase, #1 at 2026 Wealthies, and being featured across the industry.

 

We're based in Chelsea, NYC, building fast and ambitious systems at the intersection of data, AI, and real-world wealth services.

 


ABOUT THE TEAM

 

You'll join FINNY Engineering and report to our VP of Engineering. The team today is product and backend engineers and a data team. You'll be our first analytics engineer, building the foundation of the company's analytics warehouse on dbt Core and Snowflake.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

 

FINNY is a metrics-driven company. Until now, our analytics warehouse has been a shared role, divided across several teams. We're bringing it together in a new structure, on a new foundation, and we're hiring a senior Analytics Engineer to own it end to end: the models, the definitions of the metrics the company runs on, and the reports people trust.

 

You'll work directly with operations, sales, marketing, growth strategy, finance, product and engineering. Success looks like: the metrics the company runs on have tested definitions, a small set of reports is the first place people look, AI tools answer questions about those metrics correctly, and every key business area is covered to the same standard. As the data team grows, you'll help hire and lead it.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the analytics warehouse day to day: staging and core models, dimensions, facts and identity resolution across our systems

 - Define the metrics FINNY runs on, with tests and documentation, so every team works from the same numbers

 - Partner with internal stakeholders across the company to turn their questions into models and reports they use

 - Own the BI layer: choose the tool and semantic layer, and keep a small set of authoritative reports

 - Make the warehouse something AI tools can answer from correctly

 - Run the dbt project like software: version control, code review, CI, tests and documentation

 


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Typically 4+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering or analytics, including owning models that other teams relied on

 - Strong SQL and dimensional modeling: facts, dimensions, conformed keys, and a clear grain for every table

 - dbt (or an equivalent tool) in production, with git, tests and CI

 - You've defined business metrics people used to make decisions, and fixed the cause when two numbers disagreed

 - You work directly with non-technical partners and turn vague questions into clear answers—and say "not yet" with a reason

 - Scrappy, with ownership: you jump in where help is needed, including work outside your job description

 - You're excited to work in person, 5 days a week, in our Chelsea, NYC office

 


NICE TO HAVE

 - First or early data hire at a startup

 - Modeled complex pricing, billing, subscription or usage data

 - Made data usable by AI agents: documentation, a semantic layer, guardrails

 - Event analytics (PostHog or similar) and CRM data

 


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

FINNY offers a competitive compensation package including:

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance

 - Flexible paid time off

 - 401(k)

 - Food and meals provided in our NYC office

 - Team offsites and events\

 - Set performance targets and allocate investment based on pipeline, CAC, channel efficiency, and revenue

 - Partner closely with Sales, RevOps, Product Marketing to ensure a tight feedback loop on ICPs, lead quality, SLAs and pipeline handoff process

 - Use AI and automation to increase the speed and quality of campaign development, analysis, and experimentation

 - Identify, test, and scale growth channels beyond paid acquisition, turning the most promising opportunities into repeatable growth engines




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 5+ years of experience in performance marketing, growth marketing, or demand generation, ideally at a fast-growing B2B technology company

 - A strong track record of personally building and scaling paid social programs, with deep expertise in Meta

 - Strong paid search experience and fluency across the acquisition funnel, from media and creative through conversion and measurement

 - Experience owning meaningful budgets and making investment decisions based on pipeline quality, marginal efficiency, and growth potential

 - A history of managing toward qualified pipeline and revenue, not just leads, clicks, or platform-reported conversions

 - Strong analytical and creative instincts, with the ability to turn customer insight and performance data into clear hypotheses and compelling campaigns

 - Broad growth experience and the ability to build, test, and scale channels beyond paid media

About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform, where people trade on the outcomes of real-world events. As our markets, volumes, and derivative product suite grow, so does the sophistication of the risk infrastructure behind them. Our clearing and risk systems must operate with the rigor of a traditional clearinghouse while moving at the speed of a crypto-native trading platform.



The Role

We're hiring a mid-level quantitative risk analyst to design and implement enterprise-scale risk models at the heart of our clearing operation. You'll own models for market risk, volatility and correlation of derivatives, stress testing, and automated liquidation — the systems that keep the platform solvent and users protected in fast-moving markets.

This is a hands-on role: you'll be building models in production code, not just specifying them. We expect you to work fluently with AI tools for development and research — and to be the skeptic in the room, pressure-testing AI-generated models and code against well-established risk frameworks before anything ships.



What You'll Do

 - Design, implement, and maintain enterprise-scale risk models covering market risk, margin, and counterparty exposure for a clearing organization.

 - Build volatility and correlation models for derivatives, including calibration, backtesting, and ongoing model validation.

 - Develop and run stress-testing frameworks: historical scenarios, hypothetical shocks, and reverse stress tests.

 - Design and tune auto-liquidation logic — trigger thresholds, liquidation waterfalls, and safeguards against cascading liquidations.

 - Use AI tools extensively to accelerate model development, coding, and research — and rigorously validate AI outputs against established risk models (VaR/ES, SPAN-style margining, GARCH-family volatility models, standard correlation frameworks) before deployment.

 - Monitor model performance in production, investigate breaks, and iterate quickly.

 - Partner with engineering, trading, and product teams to embed risk controls into platform architecture.

 - Document model assumptions, limitations, and validation results to an audit-ready standard.
   
   

What We're Looking For

 - 5–7 years of quantitative risk experience at a clearinghouse, exchange, prime broker, trading firm, or similar.

 - Proven expertise designing and implementing risk models at enterprise scale — production systems, not just research prototypes.

 - Deep experience modeling volatility, correlation, option skews, option pricing and implementing at scale for trad-fi derivatives, perpetuals, and fully collateralized event contracts.

 - Hands-on experience with market risk modeling, stress testing, and auto-liquidation mechanics in a clearing context.

 - Strong fluency with AI-assisted development and coding, paired with the judgment to pressure-test AI outputs against well-established risk models and catch what looks plausible but is wrong.

 - Expert-level Python (numerical stack: NumPy, pandas, SciPy; solid software engineering practices).

 - Advanced degree in a quantitative field (math, statistics, physics, financial engineering, CS) or equivalent experience.

 - Strong mathematical foundation in stochastic calculus and linear algebra.



Nice to Have

 - C# and/or C++ for performance-critical or production systems.

 - Familiarity with crypto market structure, perpetuals, or prediction markets.

 - Experience with CCP risk frameworks (CPMI-IOSCO PFMI, default management, margin methodology).

 - Experience building real-time risk systems.



Location & Work Setup

This role is based in our New York City office, in person. You'll be working directly alongside the trading, engineering, and risk teams.

ABOUT ARKETA

Arketa is building the operating system for modern fitness and wellness. Studio owners run their whole business on Arketa, from bookings and payments to payroll and marketing. Internally, we run the company on AI agents connected to every system we use, so a lean team moves like a much bigger one. We're writing the playbook for how a modern company operates, and bringing that same AI to the studios we serve.

We're growing fast. We're also one of the most AI-forward teams you'll find: ideas go from whiteboard to live in days, not quarters.





ABOUT THE ROLE

This role is for someone who wants to build one of the most in-demand skills in business: running AI agents on real sales and marketing problems. You'll see how a fast-growing tech company works from the inside, ship things the team uses every day, and leave each project with proof of what you built. It's a fast way into tech, with paths into sales, marketing, product, or operations, and a skill set that compounds.

We have a lot of high-impact go-to-market projects. They need someone deeply analytical who moves fast, thinks creatively, and has real hustle. You'll work directly with our CEO, picking up whatever matters most to sales and marketing that month.

The honest version: this job is about 10% strategy and 90% execution. You'll be an agent orchestrator. You'll set up the data and infrastructure, build the skills and agents that do the work, and wire up automations so things run without you.



What that looks like in practice. Say we want to know what separates a demo that closes from one that doesn't, and coach every rep toward it. You would:

 1. Connect call recordings and demo notes to HubSpot, define the fields that matter (pain points, objections, next steps), and make sure every demo is captured cleanly.

 2. Build a skill that scores each demo against what our best reps do, then an agent that runs it on every new call and surfaces patterns by rep, segment, and deal stage.

 3. Set up an automation that pings the sales manager when a rep's demo quality drops below a threshold, with the calls and coaching points attached.

Then you track whether close rates move, tune the system, and hand it off to run on its own. Then you do it again for the next problem.




WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

To start, everything is go-to-market. The agents you build could live in sales or marketing. Some of the questions you might own:

 - How do we rotate ad creative faster, at higher quality, and learn which concepts work?

 - How do we ramp new sellers faster?

 - What separates a demo that closes from one that doesn't, and how do we coach to it?

 - Which marketing channels drive pipeline that actually closes?

You'll get a defined first project on day one. Over time, you'll take on a set of weekly responsibilities and own them end to end.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - 30 days: Learn our sales and marketing motion, sit in on demos, and ship your first working automation.

 - 60 days: Own a full project, from data setup to a live agent the team relies on.

 - 90 days: Show measurable movement on a GTM metric, and run several projects with little direction.
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 1 to 3 years at a top consulting, private equity, or banking firm

 - Sharp, structured thinking: you break a messy problem into parts and get to a defensible answer fast

 - A builder's instinct: you've shipped things yourself, not just written the deck

 - Daily use of AI tools, with your own view on what works

 - Clear, direct communication, and you take feedback well

 - Ability to work from our NoHo office 3 days a week

Bonus: exposure to sales or marketing, hands-on experience with automation tools or a CRM like HubSpot, and an interest in fitness, wellness, or small businesses.




YOU SHOULD APPLY IF

 - You want to be at the top of your game and learn faster than anywhere else

ABOUT POLYMARKET

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast — both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The Growth team owns how Polymarket acquires users and converts attention into volume. We move fast, spend real money across a range of channels and geographies, and hold ourselves to business outcomes — not vanity metrics. The media investment function sits at the center of that, and right now it needs someone who can build the analytical backbone that makes every dollar accountable.

This is not a coordination role. You will own the media plan, the forecast, the measurement approach, and the reconciliation. Polymarket operates in an event-driven, highly seasonal environment where timing and pricing can matter as much as budget size — we're looking for someone genuinely restless about finding edge, willing to go looking for the insight nobody asked for and kill their own conclusion when the data doesn't hold.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build the media plan across channels, categories, and geographies, and present a clear, defensible recommendation with tradeoffs and a point of view — not a menu of options

 - Own the forecasting layer covering spend, volume, acquisition cost, payback, and seasonality, and maintain scenario models that make tradeoffs legible before capital is committed; when we miss a forecast, explain why and make the next model better

 - Pace spend daily and weekly against approved allocations, flag over and under delivery early enough to act, and surface when the actual channel or geographic mix has drifted from the approved plan

 - Lead the measurement approach across mix modeling, incrementality testing, and geographic experiments, and synthesize the outputs into one defensible view of what is working rather than four competing ones

 - Reconcile every media dollar spent, tying platform spend to invoices, agency billing, and the finance ledger, and own accruals, credits, make-goods, and discrepancy resolution through monthly close

 - Hunt continuously for edge in auction dynamics, underpriced inventory, seasonality patterns, and competitive activity, and recommend in-flight reallocation with evidence when the data supports it

 - Build the reporting and analytics layer the team runs on, including dashboards, metric definitions, and a single source of truth that holds up under scrutiny from finance and leadership
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 6+ years in media planning, marketing analytics, or growth strategy with real ownership of plans and numbers — not just supporting roles

 - Deep fluency across paid channels including search, social, programmatic, video, audio, and offline, sufficient to pressure test a buyer's recommendation on the substance

 - Strong quantitative foundation in forecasting and scenario modeling; strong SQL and comfort in BI tooling — you build your own analysis rather than waiting for someone else to pull the data

 - Hands-on experience with mix modeling, incrementality testing, and geographic experiments, and the intellectual honesty to be clear about what each method can and cannot tell you

 - Financial rigor and comfort owning a number that has to tie out, including reconciliation, accruals, and working directly with finance through monthly close

 - Demonstrated ability to compress a complex analysis into a one-page recommendation an executive can act

ABOUT THE ROLE

Commure's finance team is rebuilding revenue accounting from the ground up, and this role is the architect of that rebuild. We're creating a brand-new Manager, Revenue Accounting & Deal Operations position to do two things at once: stand up our deal desk function from scratch, and modernize the technical infrastructure that supports revenue recognition across a fast-growing, multi-product healthcare technology business.



This isn't a maintain-the-status-quo role. You'll be the primary accounting owner of deal desk — building the process, the playbooks, and the cross-functional muscle memory with Sales, Legal, and Revenue Operations that doesn't yet exist at scale. In parallel, you'll partner with our broader revenue accounting team on close, reconciliations, and audit support, and you'll have real influence over which tools and automation we adopt to get there. Our finance team invests aggressively in emerging finance technology, and you'll have the opportunity to engage in the debate and build out around how AI and automation should change the way revenue accounting and deal desk work gets done.



If you want to build something from a blank page rather than inherit a finished process, and you want a direct hand in shaping how a scaling, IPO-track company runs deal desk and revenue accounting, this is that seat.




WHAT YOU'LL DO


DEAL DESK & PROCESS OWNERSHIP

 - Build our deal desk function. Design and build the finance deal desk from the ground up — intake, deal structuring support, approval workflows, and documentation — in close partnership with Sales, Legal, and Revenue Operations.

 - Set the playbook. Create the frameworks, templates, and guardrails that let Sales structure deals quickly while keeping revenue recognition, pricing, and contractual risk in check.

 - Be the go-to accounting voice on deal structuring. Advise on non-standard terms, bundled arrangements, and complex pricing models in real time, before deals are finalized — not after.

We're looking for a Revenue Operations Lead to own the systems, data, and rhythm behind Peec's global revenue engine. We've grown from $0 to $15M ARR in 18 months on a motion that combines product-led signups with a fast-scaling sales team across Berlin and New York, and the operational layer now needs a single owner: one source of truth in the CRM, a forecast leadership can trust across both regions, and automation that lets a lean GTM team punch far above its weight.

ABOUT ABRIDGE

Founded in 2018, Abridge is the first AI-native clinician intelligence platform organized around the patient, built for clinicians, and designed to help health systems coordinate the clinical, financial, and evidence-based decisions for every moment of care. Powered by purpose-built AI for healthcare, Abridge connects patients, providers, payers, and life sciences companies. This year, the platform will support more than 100 million patient-clinician conversations across more than 300 of the largest and most complex health systems in the U.S. With deep workflow integration, the Abridge clinician intelligence platform has been validated to support encounters in 28+ languages across specialties and care settings.

Abridge is setting the industry standard for the responsible deployment of Al across health systems with continual and transparent Al evaluation. Clinical decision support references and cites gold-standard sources of evidence, and features like Linked Evidence map AI-generated documentation to source data, helping clinicians quickly trust and verify the output.

Abridge was awarded Best in KLAS for Ambient AI in 2025 and 2026, in addition to other accolades, including TIME Best Inventions of 2024 and 2025, CNBC Disruptor 2025, and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies 2025.

We are a growing team of practicing clinicians, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to transform healthcare. We have offices located in San Francisco, New York, and Pittsburgh.




THE ROLE

Abridge is growing from one product into a platform, creating new ways to serve health systems and reach different buyers. Each opportunity brings choices about the offer and the commercial motion that will make it work.

You will own those choices for a focused set of commercial priorities, from the first hypothesis through a tested recommendation. You will determine which buyers to pursue and build an offer around the problem they need to solve. Pricing and packaging will be central to that work, alongside the economic case and the path to a sale.

This is a senior individual contributor role on the Commercial Strategy team. You will do the analysis and write the first draft yourself, working closely with colleagues who bring product expertise and customer context. Your work should give leadership a clear decision and give the field an offer a buyer can understand and carry forward internally.

You will carry each body of work through an initial test and a clear handoff to the teams responsible for execution. The role requires commercial judgment and the ability to finish work that others can use.

About BiOptimizers

BiOptimizers exist to help people go from baseline health to peak biological performance. We develop science-backed supplements and wellness tools that deliver measurable results. As a remote-first company, our globally distributed team focuses on clarity, autonomy, and operational excellence. Every role is designed to support the health and performance of both our customers and our organization.



About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Innovation Operations Manager to lead the exploration and evaluation of new product and business opportunities that extend beyond our core competency of creating and commercializing capsule and powder dietary supplements across categories such as minerals, digestion, and more. This role will also manage the operations aspect of all new products, allowing us to get the products to commercialization stage. 

This is a highly cross-functional role for a natural investigator and organizer—someone who can take an early-stage innovation concept, dig into its technical and commercial feasibility, engage the right internal and external partners, and provide stakeholders with clear, evidence-based recommendations on whether a concept can be successfully commercialized and made profitable, or whether it should be shelved.

If you thrive on ambiguity, love connecting the dots between science, operations, and market opportunity, and can drive structured decision-making, we'd love to hear from you.

This role exists specifically to handle novel, high-ambiguity concepts — the ideas that fall outside what we already know how to make. Just as important as finding the winners is closing out the losers. We are looking for someone who reaches a defensible answer quickly and is comfortable recommending that we stop. A fast, well-evidenced “no” is a successful outcome in this role, not a failure — concepts that sit in permanent exploration are the specific problem this role is being created to solve.

Key Responsibilities

 - Research & Investigate: Identify, research, and investigate new innovation ideas and concepts to assess their technical and commercial feasibility, including opportunities outside our existing product formats and categories.

 - Collaborate with R&D & Formulators: Work closely with our formulators and R&D teams to deeply understand each innovation concept, its scientific underpinnings, and its technical requirements and constraints.

 - Conduct Feasibility Analyses: Design and execute structured feasibility analyses covering technical viability, manufacturability, cost, regulatory considerations, timelines, and commercial potential.

 - Source & Manage External Partners: Identify, vet, and manage relationships with external parties—such as vendors, contract manufacturers, labs, consultants, and specialists—to fill capability gaps and validate concepts. Prepare RFQs and manage the quote and aware process with contract manufacturers.

 - Enable Decision-Making: Synthesize findings into clear business cases and recommendations that help stakeholders determine whether a concept can be commercialized profitably or should be deemed unviable.

 - Manage Projects End-to-End: Own project plans, timelines, budgets, milestones, and stakeholder communications across multiple concurrent innovation initiatives. This is a hands-on, in-the-weeds role with no supporting staff — you will personally do the research, build the models, chase the vendors, and run the trials.

 - Report & Communicate: Present findings, risks, and recommendations to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders in a clear, actionable format.

 - Own the Innovation Intake Queue: Serve as the single point of entry for concepts from any source — founders, leadership, R&D, or the field. Log every idea, run a fast initial screen, and work with leadership to maintain a ranked, capacity-bound queue with an agreed limit on how many concepts are under active investigation at once.

 - Proven track record successfully managing upmarket concurrent implementation projects without compromising quality, customer experience, or timelines

About Imagine Worldwide
 All children have immense potential, but hundreds of millions don’t have access to the learning they need. Imagine Worldwide believes that every child should be empowered with the basic right to literacy and numeracy. We provide an innovative education technology solution and implementation model to the global literacy/numeracy learning crisis using the onebillion application and various toolkits and systems to support implementation. Our model is massively scalable, evidence-based, and can deliver foundational learning to millions of the most marginalized children.
 Imagine Worldwide partners with governments, organizations, and communities to provide child-directed, tablet-based learning that is accessible, effective, and affordable. We are incorporated in California (United States) as a nonprofit organization, but operate in Sub-Saharan Africa through locally-registered entities in Malawi, Sierra Leone, and Tanzania. Learn more on our website .
 Role Overview
 The Senior Analytics Engineer builds, runs and improves Imagine’s analytics platform: the infrastructure, pipelines and core data models that the organisation’s reporting and analysis depend on. The central task is to scale the platform as data volumes grow, keeping costs under control without giving up performance. In a small team, that means covering the infrastructure underneath the data as well as the data engineering itself.
 Imagine’s data comes from many sources. The largest is tablets in more than 1,500 schools across Malawi, Tanzania and Sierra Leone, which record learning activity as individual events, adding up to billions of records. These only become meaningful when joined with programme context, such as active schools per term, device allocations and enrolment, and with operational data from inventory and field data collection. Turning all of this into reliable data on a non-profit budget calls for careful decisions about where processing happens and what each workload costs.
 The role reports to the Director of Analytics, who sets the platform’s architecture and technical standards, and works alongside the rest of the Analytics Team. We are looking for someone senior who takes initiative, turns architectural direction into working systems, and brings forward evidence-based proposals for improving them. As the engineer builds context, they take on increasing ownership of the platform’s day-to-day running and technical decisions.
 Key Responsibilities
 The Senior Analytics Engineer’s responsibilities fall into four pillars. The first two cover the platform itself: the infrastructure it runs on, and the pipelines that bring data in from many sources and process it at scale. The third covers orchestration and the core data models that the rest of the Analytics Team builds on. The fourth covers the practices that keep the platform reliable, secure and affordable to run.
 Data Platform and Infrastructure 
 Imagine’s analytics platform runs on AWS and ClickHouse Cloud, with infrastructure managed as code. In a small team, this role carries the infrastructure work that a larger organisation would split across dedicated platform or DevOps staff, limited to the scope of the analytics platform.
- Build and maintain the platform’s AWS infrastructure, including storage, compute, networking, the data catalogue, secrets and access management (S3, EC2, Glue Data Catalog, Lake Formation, IAM, Secrets Manager).
- Manage infrastructure as code in Terraform, keeping environments reproducible, version-controlled and reviewable.
- Administer the ClickHouse Cloud warehouse, including service configuration, user and role management, and monitoring of performance and capacity.
- Host and maintain the team’s self-hosted tools, including Apache Superset for BI and Apache Airflow for orchestration. This covers deployment, upgrades, authentication and availability. The Senior BI & Data Analyst manages the dashboards and content within Superset

Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam.
 We’re hiring a Claims Analyst to own the day-to-day integrity of our claims and adjudication workflows and to help build the processes, controls, and reporting behind them. This is a hands-on role: you’ll personally work our hardest claims and denials while standing up the playbooks, benchmarks, and dashboards that let claims operations scale without breaking. Reporting to our Manager, RCM, you’ll sit at the intersection of our clearinghouse, prior-auth, and finance systems — and you’ll be the person who can explain exactly why a claim paid, denied, or landed where it did.
 What you'll do: 
- Own claims adjudication and QA. Review, validate, and adjudicate imaging claims against benefit designs, contracted rates, and our pass-through payment model; identify and resolve pricing, coding, and eligibility discrepancies before they become client or member issues.
- Lead denials management. Investigate root causes of denials and underpayments, drive appeals and resubmissions, and build recurring analysis that turns denial patterns into fixes upstream (prior auth, eligibility, EDI configuration).
- Manage EDI and clearinghouse workflows. Work hands-on in Waystar across 837P submissions, 835 remittances, and companion-guide requirements; troubleshoot rejections and payer-specific edits; partner with vendors to keep the pipes clean.
- Safeguard cost-share and accumulator accuracy. Ensure deductible, coinsurance, HDHP, and accumulator logic is applied correctly so members and clients are billed accurately and we stay compliant with cost-sharing rules.
- Own AR and aging. Monitor accounts receivable and claims aging, prioritize collectible balances, and maintain reporting that gives finance and leadership a real-time view of what’s outstanding and why.
- Build the reporting layer. Develop and maintain dashboards and KPIs (adjudication turnaround, denial rate, clean-claim rate, AR aging, recovery rate) from Waystar and adjacent claims data.
- Coordinate across the stack. Work closely with prior authorization (Infinx), finance, and client-facing teams to close the loop between authorization, exam, claim, and payment.
- Write the playbook. Document repeatable SOPs, edits, and escalation paths, and help train and mentor analysts as the team grows.
 About you: 
 Required 
- 2+ years in healthcare claims, revenue cycle, or medical billing, with demonstrated ownership of complex adjudication and denials work
- Deep hands-on experience with EDI transactions (837/835) and a clearinghouse platform (Waystar strongly preferred)
- Strong command of CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10, place-of-service, and modifier logic — ideally in radiology/imaging
- Working knowledge of benefit structures, cost-sharing, deductibles, and accumulator/HDHP mechanics
- Advanced spreadsheet skills and comfort building reporting from raw claims data
- A meticulous, audit-minded approach: you can trace any dollar to its source and defend it
 Preferred 
- Experience at a TPA, benefits administrator, or payer, especially serving self-funded employers
- Familiarity with prior authorization workflows and tools (e.g., Infinx)
- Exposure to appeals, payer escalations, and underpayment recovery at scale
- Early-stage or high-growth environment experience — comfortable building process where none exists
 The salary range for this position is $50,000 -

- Gather customer requirements and design PLEXOS-based modeling solutions, either enhancing existing datasets or building models from scratch.

 Aegis Ventures is a next-generation startup studio that partners with entrepreneurs and industry leaders to originate, launch, and scale transformative companies, with a focus on artificial intelligence. The Aegis platform brings together market-shaping ideas, permanent growth capital, and ambitious individuals who are driven to solve major societal problems.  Optain  is a revolutionary healthcare company that uses groundbreaking software and hardware technology to rethink care. We use the eye as a window to the body to improve the way we detect and manage eye and systemic conditions. Optain is committed to expanding and improving care through the introduction of AI and machine learning technology frontline care settings at an accessible price. This not only promotes greater access to care, but promises to reduce the strains of overburdened healthcare systems. 
 Originally founded in Australia in 2019, Optain seeks to commercialize the inventions of Professor Mingguang He, a preeminent clinician-scientist and scholar in the field of ophthalmology. Optain has achieved regulatory approval and commercial adoption of its product suite in global markets, including Australia, Europe, and more.

These systems collectively deliver care to 28 million patients across 25 states and have begun deploying Optain's platform across their networks, rapidly accelerating the company's footprint and expanding screening access nationwide.  As the Clinical Operations Manager , you will own the operations of Optain's provider network -- the optometrists and ophthalmologists who read retinal images for health systems, clinics, and community health centers across the United States. The network has run for 15 years on the judgment and relationships of a small number of people. Your job is to turn that into documented policy, a measurable quality program, a capacity model that runs ahead of demand, and a governance rhythm in alignment with Optain’s Medical Director. You will report to the VP of Operations and work day to day with Optain's Medical Director. This is a non-clinical role for someone who has managed a network of contracted clinicians before, writes policy that physicians sign, and knows the difference between running a process and building one that doesn't need you.
 Optain is at an inflection point. We have FDA clearance, a growing camera footprint, and a commercial pipeline that is moving fast. Behind every screening exam is a licensed grader reading the images through our EyePACS platform, and the operational infrastructure around that network is being built in real time. This role sits at the center of that work.
 This is a remote, US-based position.

- Own the grading playbook, SOPs, onboarding materials, and the provider network policy library -- author, version, and maintain them, and route clinical content to the Medical Director for review and sign-off.

 Counterpart is an insurtech platform reimagining management and professional liability for the modern workplace. We believe that when businesses lead with clarity and confidence, they become more resilient, more innovative, and better prepared for what's ahead. That's why we  built the first Agentic Insurance™ system, where advanced AI and deep insurance expertise come together to proactively assess, mitigate, and manage risk. Backed by A rated carriers and trusted by brokers nationwide, our platform helps small businesses grow with confidence.
 You'll build the systems and conditions that let a small team run a national platform: hunting bottlenecks, removing them, and making sure they don't come back, so product, underwriting, and engineering can move at the pace the company needs.
 This role touches every part of how an insurance product works (coverage language, pricing, filings, distribution) and every part of how an AI native company runs. What we're looking for is operational rigor: relentless follow through, quick learning, and the judgment to keep a cross functional team on track and moving efficiently, no matter how complex the surface area gets.
   HOW YOU OPERATE 
- Find the biggest bottleneck in a function, fix it, then move to the next one. You'll be judged on how many you clear, not how many you document.
- Remove unnecessary steps before adding new ones.
- Use AI daily in your own work. You should be one of the heaviest AI users in the company.
 Own New Product Launches, End to End 
- Lead new product launches from kickoff to the point where they run on their own, without you day to day.
- Translate product strategy into clear specifications for pricing, data, and engineering, so requirements don't get lost or reinterpreted.
- Set the build order with engineering and data, and hold that order when priorities compete.
 Turn Expert Judgment Into Systems 
- Build a simple way for underwriting and pricing experts to enter their own rules and judgment into our systems, so they don't need to route through you.
- Keep terminology consistent across every system, model, and team, and update it as the business grows.
- Set up fast, accurate feedback from policies, claims, and lost deals, so we know quickly what's working and what needs to change.
 Own Change Control and Quality 
- Create and run one clear process for any change to what we sell (coverage, rules, pricing), so changes don't happen ad hoc.
- Catch problems in testing before they reach a customer.
- Move existing programs onto shared infrastructure instead of maintaining separate one off setups.
 YOU HAVE 
- 7+ years solving complex problems through process and product development, or a clear track record of taking on more scope and responsibility over time.
- A systems thinker who obsesses over problems and builds solutions that scale, rather than one off fixes.
- Exceptional project management and documentation skills, with the ability to run multiple workstreams at once without dropping detail.
- A self starter mindset: comfortable rolling up your sleeves in a lean, fast moving environment.
- Real, daily comfort working with AI agents (delegating to them, checking their work, improving them). You automate a task the second time you do it, not the tenth.
- Evidence of grit: something you've pushed through more than once, even when it would have been easier to stop.
- Insurance background is a plus, not a requirement. If you have exposure to policy forms, rate and rule filings, or systems like SERFF, that's a bonus, not a prerequisite.
 WHO YOU WILL WORK WITH:

About GiveDirectly   
 What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?
 Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.
 Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty? 
 We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join. 
 We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.
 How we work 
 Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:
- Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.
- Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.
- Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.
- Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.
- Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.
- Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.
- Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.
- Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.
 If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.
 Want to learn more? Read and listen: 
 We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist , NPR , TED , and The Washington Post . We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.
 About this role 
 GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to more than 2 million people living in poverty across 15 countries. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up.
 We are growing at an unprecedented scale. By the end of 2027, we will have more than tripled dollars delivered via our current playbook to $750M+, while building toward a step-change of roughly 10x on a new technology stack and operating model. We also believe that we could deliver significant incremental money through external partnerships, whether by sourcing verified lists from an institutional partner like UNHCR, subgranting to partners with existing distribution capacity, or routing funds directly through an established remittance provider.

About GiveDirectly   
 What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?
 Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.
 Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty? 
 We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join. 
 We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.
 How we work 
 Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:
- Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.
- Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.
- Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.

- Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.
- Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.
- Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.
 If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.
 Want to learn more? Read and listen: 
 We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist , NPR , TED , and The Washington Post . We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

 At Gigs, we're building the operating system for mobile services—a platform that lets tech companies embed global connectivity into their products effortlessly.
 Just as Stripe lets any business add a payment button in seconds, Gigs empowers platforms to weave in connectivity—bridging the traditional world of telecom with modern tech. From fintechs launching mobile services to HR platforms offering work phone plans, we automate provisioning and remove telecom complexity.
 Our team of around 150 people across the US and Europe, backed by nearly $100 million in funding from Ribbit Capital, Google, and Y Combinator. As one of the fastest-growing tech companies, bringing together early-stage engineers, product builders, and business athletes from companies like Stripe, Airbnb, and Shopify. We’re tackling deep technical and regulatory challenges to make connectivity truly seamless.
 If you’re driven by curiosity, creativity, and the chance to shape the future of telecom, we’d love to hear from you.
 Things We Care About 
 We are building in a highly complex space and tackling a massive problem. We want people who lean in when things get hard.
- Speed. We move and we ship. We set bold deadlines and treat every week like it matters.
- Ownership. If you see something broken, fix it. We don't wait for permission.
- Customer Obsession . Our customers' product is our product.
- Ambiguity. We're building frontier technology in a complex domain. You'll need sound judgement and good instincts to make decisions without complete information.
- First principles. We don't ask how things have been done before. We ask why they were done that way at all.
 The Role
 GTM Associates at Gigs are the engine of top-of-funnel growth - and the starting point for a career in commercial leadership. You'll work closely with GTM Leads to identify, qualify, and develop pipeline across Gigs' markets.
 This isn't a role where you execute a handed-to-you playbook. You'll help build it and the best people here grow fast because of it. Our GTM org is lean by design. You'll have real visibility with GTM leadership from day one, and the commercial decisions you make will matter.
 What you will do 
- You'll become a product expert. You'll develop deep knowledge of the Gigs platform and our competitor landscape - understanding not just what we offer, but why it matters to each buyer and how we win.
- You'll own both inbound and outbound. You'll manage inbound leads using clear qualifying criteria and prospect into new accounts with strategic, thoughtful outreach to upmarket buyers. Quality of engagement matters as much as volume.
- You'll bring AI into how you work, naturally. You research accounts, prepare for meetings, and iterate on outreach using AI tools as a core part of your workflow. You share what works and help raise the bar for how the whole team operates.
- You'll partner with marketing to drive pipeline. You'll work closely with the marketing team to manage outbound campaigns, increase lead volume, and make sure commercial follow-through is tight when campaigns land.
- You'll prepare every conversation to a high standard. Before any meeting, you know the company, the buyer, and the angle. You develop the instincts to match research to relevance - and you use every tool available to get there faster.
- You'll keep the CRM your source of truth. You'll maintain accurate, up-to-date records in HubSpot so that the whole team can act on clean data. Good hygiene isn't admin - it's how the machine runs.
- You'll provide deal support and develop judgment alongside experienced operators. You'll shadow deal calls, run discovery meetings, and progressively take on more ownership as your skills develop.
- You'll contribute to strategic projects across the US GTM org. Pipeline is your anchor, but this role is deliberately broader. You'll flex into market mapping, go-to-market experiments, and commercial analysis as the US team scales

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences. 
 Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right? 
 To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!
Ready to be part of the experience? 
 Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.
 DATES 
 Start: 9/21/2026
 End: 1/9/2027
 Approximately six days per week and hours are typically 14:00 – 23:30 plus meetings and reporting work.
 Working from home for the prep period before install.
 Working onsite for the load in, event run, and strike.
 PAY RATE  
 $350/day
 ABOUT THE ROLE 
 The Retail Performance Manager reports directly to the Event Manager and Global Retail Lead and is responsible for the day-to-day running of all HPFFE retail stores.
 This role combines retail leadership, commercial performance, and operational execution. The Retail Performance Manager has full ownership of store performance, team management, stock control, Square POS accuracy, add-on fulfillment operations, and the timely load-in and load-out of all retail operations.
 The Retail Performance Manager will ensure a seamless, high-quality guest experience while maximizing revenue, maintaining strong operational standards, and following processes established by the Global Team.
 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Store Operations
- Oversee the daily running of all onsite retail stores.
- Ensure a smooth, efficient, and commercially optimized guest retail journey.
- Maintain high operational, presentation, cleanliness, and guest-service standards at all times.
- Act as the primary onsite point of contact for retail operations.
- Ensure effective day-to-day use of Square POS devices across all retail locations.

- Verify that fixtures, shelving, storage, lighting, and other infrastructure are correctly installed, functional, and fit for purpose.

- Liaise with the Props team to coordinate prop installation once retail areas are fully set up and ready for access.

- Work with a Fever Ops team member to ensure all systems and processes are correctly set up in line with Global Team requirements.
- Oversee Back-of-House setup to ensure stock is stored safely, logically, and accessibly, with shelving correctly installed and used.
- Oversee storage-container setup, ensuring shelving is correctly installed, containers are clearly labeled, and stock is loaded and stored safely in line with agreed guidelines.
- Implement a clear stock-control tracking process for each storage container.
- Ensure all products are correctly merchandised, clearly labeled, and priced in accordance with agreed guidelines.

About Modo Energy 
 The energy transition is the biggest infrastructure buildout in human history. Modo Energy is the data platform at the centre of it.
 We build the benchmarking, forecasting, and valuation tools that the world's most serious energy investors, developers, and operators depend on to make decisions. If a battery gets financed, built, or traded anywhere in the world, there's a good chance Modo Energy's data was in the room.
 Founded in 2019, we're 90+ people across London, New York, Sydney, and Madrid; $30M Series B, AI-native, and moving fast.
 This is a rare chance to join a category-defining company at the moment it's scaling globally.

 Market Analyst, Modeling (CAISO / SPP)
 Reports to: US Modeling Lead
 Team: Modeling
 Regions: Western Interconnection - CAISO / SPP
 About the role
 Modo Energy's models tell clients where to build assets, how they will operate, and what they are worth. This role builds them.
 The work spans capacity expansion, dispatch and price models, all running inside the Modo Energy platform. You will own a piece of it: a market, a model, or a part of the stack, and take it from a question about how the market behaves through to code that runs in production.
 What you will do
- Build models. Write and maintain the dispatch, price and capacity expansion models for the markets you cover.
- Learn your markets. Know how your ISOs clear energy and ancillary services, and what changed last month.
- Test your own work. Backtest against market outturn, find where the model is wrong, and fix it.
- Explain the results. Show colleagues and clients why the model produced the number it produced.
- Work with other teams: 
- Research - take their read on what is changing in the market and build it into what you model.
- Engineering - tell them what the modeling stack needs. You are the user of what they build.
- Revenue - join technical sales and post-sales calls when clients want to understand the method.
 What you need
- Degree in engineering, maths, physics, economics, or a related field
- 2+ years in power market modeling, analytics, or a quantitative role in energy
- You write Python that other people can run, and you work in git
- You can write and debug an optimization problem — unit commitment, dispatch, or similar
- You know how at least one US power market clears energy and ancillary services
- You can take a vague question about market behavior and turn it into something you can model
- You say when a result looks wrong rather than shipping it
 Nice to have
- Experience with battery storage dispatch or revenue modeling
- Experience with an optimization library such as Linopy, Pyomo or PuLP
- Experience with nodal pricing, PTDFs, or transmission-constrained dispatch
- Experience working with large time series datasets in SQL

Prosper Health is on a mission to make life happier and healthier for autistic and neurodivergent adults. 
 Despite autism diagnoses increasing more than 5x in the past 25 years, autistic adults have been systematically overlooked. This has led to extremely poor outcomes, including high rates of co-occurring mental health conditions and a lower life expectancy. Prosper is here to change that. 
 We deliver specialized mental health services for autistic adults, covered by insurance. We've helped tens of thousands of people receive an autism diagnosis for the first time, work with neurodivergent-affirming therapists, and find belonging through community. Our outcomes meaningfully outperform traditional care for autistic adults, with substantially greater improvements in mood, anxiety, and quality of life.

 Good Inside is seeking a Senior Analytics Engineer to own the data foundation behind our product.  This is a full stack role, weighted toward analytics engineering. You'll design production-grade dbt models for product events and subscription data, own our Amplitude instrumentation and tracking plans, and keep data fresh, tested, and trusted. Because you'll sit close to Product, you'll also turn that foundation into analysis, experiment readouts, and recommendations, using statistical methods when a question needs more than a dashboard.

Prosper Health is on a mission to make life happier and healthier for autistic and neurodivergent adults. 
 Despite autism diagnoses increasing more than 5x in the past 25 years, autistic adults have been systematically overlooked. This has led to extremely poor outcomes, including high rates of co-occurring mental health conditions and a lower life expectancy. Prosper is here to change that. 
 We deliver specialized mental health services for autistic adults, covered by insurance. We've helped tens of thousands of people receive an autism diagnosis for the first time, work with neurodivergent-affirming therapists, and find belonging through community. Our outcomes meaningfully outperform traditional care for autistic adults, with substantially greater improvements in mood, anxiety, and quality of life.
 Prosper is growing 3x year over year and is at mid-double-digit millions in run-rate revenue, with thousands of active clients and 1,000+ clinicians. We're a high-ownership, mission-driven team, building something that has never existed for autistic and neurodivergent adults.
 About the Role
 Prosper is building the healthcare home for autistic and neurodivergent adults, a population that has long been underserved. Insurance coverage is one of the biggest factors in whether people can access our care, and we have a major untapped opportunity to bring Prosper in-network with more health plans and to deepen those partnerships.
 As our Strategy & Operations Lead, Commercial and Payer Partnerships , you’ll work with our Head of Commercial and Payer Partnerships to own that opportunity end-to-end. You’ll build and run our strategy for contracting with regional health plans, prioritizing which plans to target, communicating Prosper's value proposition, and negotiating agreements. You'll also own key areas of our overall commercial strategy, from how we market Prosper to payers to how we think about entering new lines of business. You'll be involved in every step of building out the commercial function for one of the fastest-growing companies in healthcare services.
 You’ll thrive here if you’re a structured thinker who loves building relationships, wants to own outcomes, and is excited to build new processes, not just manage ones someone else designed. You likely bring a mix of consulting and healthcare services experience, and you’re excited to apply that toolkit to expand access to care and drive better healthcare outcomes.
 Success in this role means: 
- Prosper is in-network with a growing set of regional and state health plans, opening care to millions more members
- Prosper is building deeper and more strategic relationships with health plans that drive greater value for both sides
- Payers know who Prosper is and why our care model matters for their members
- Our commercial engine is becoming more scalable, with processes that efficiently support go-to-market and partner success as Prosper scales to 50 states
 Key Responsibilities
- Win new payer contracts. Build and execute our strategy for regional health plans. Prioritize targets by size of opportunity, partner with Prosper leadership to identify contracts, run outreach, lead partnership discussions and negotiate agreements at competitive rates.
- Strengthen our value proposition. Work with our clinical and clinical operations teams to execute and build on our clinical quality strategy.
- Build payer awareness. Work with Prosper leadership to identify efficient, high-ROI strategies for raising awareness, including by borrowing best practices from peer companies.
- Deepen existing partnerships. Stand up a lightweight partner success model (reporting, regular check-ins, joint operating committees) and help scale it across partners.
- Make new payers work operationally. Partner with Product and Operations to build processes for seamlessly launching new payer partnerships.
- Scope what’s next. Evaluate new growth channels, such as Medicaid and direct-to-empl

- Build and maintain strong working relationships with internal teams including Data Analytics, Operations, and Technology
 Qualifications

- 1–3+ years of experience in a finance, analytics, or business operations role; residential solar, FP&A, treasury, investor relations, or utility experience strongly preferred
- Strong business acumen;  you understand how a business works and can connect financial data to operational reality

Who We Are   
 At Moxxi, we’re redefining performance marketing with cutting-edge technology and a relentless focus on results. As a profitable, bootstrapped start-up, we are led by a team of industry veterans in performance marketing, ad tech, and digital publishing. Together, we’re building the premier platform to incubate, scale, and optimize digitally born businesses, setting new standards for data-driven success.   
 Our entrepreneurial team brings proven experience from both global corporations and fast-growing startups. We’re passionate about delivering scalable, profitable outcomes for our partners through advanced profiling, targeting, and continuous optimization. Joining Moxxi means becoming part of a growing start-up in the heart of NYC, where you’ll have the opportunity to accelerate your career, expand your skill set, and shape the future of performance marketing.   
 Location: New York City
 Level: Mid-level, 3 to 5 years experience
 The Opportunity 
 As an Analytics Engineer at Moxxi, you will build and own the data models behind our marketplace reporting, and you will use them to answer questions the business has not yet figured out how to ask. This is a small analytics team, so you will not be handed a queue of tickets. You will work directly with account managers, yield, and product to understand what is actually happening in the business, then build the models and reporting that make those answers repeatable.
 A significant part of this role is applying LLMs to analytics work: connecting models to the warehouse, engineering the context they need to be useful, and building the evals that tell you whether the output can be trusted. Our Analytics Lead owns this area, and you will be a key contributor to it.
 Moxxi owns its ad server, CMS, user journey orchestration, and SMS platform, so we generate our own data and can change the systems that produce it. That also means analytics here covers both sides of the business. You will report on marketplace performance, and you will measure what product ships: how a change to a user journey affects conversion, whether a new feature did what we expected, and what that tells us to build next. You will be joining shortly after a platform migration, so expect to help define and instrument the events behind that work rather than inherit a mature measurement stack. Over time, we expect this role to grow into quantitative work on how we model and select offers.
 Responsibilities 
- Own marketplace reporting across publishers, advertisers, and verticals, and make sure the numbers the business runs on are correct.
- Build and maintain dbt models in the warehouse, with tests, in version control, shipped to production.
- Investigate anomalies end to end: what moved, why it moved, and what we should do about it.
- Apply LLMs to analytics workflows, including context engineering and evaluation, in partnership with the Analytics Lead.
- Measure product work: define success metrics for new features and journey changes, specify the events needed to track them, and report back on whether the change did what we expected.
- Partner with operators to define KPIs so the business argues about decisions rather than about whose number is right.
- Build self-service reporting so routine questions stop routing through the analytics team.
- Own data quality: reconciliation across sources, and validation that catches problems before consumers do.
- Support experimentation and measurement design as we roll out platform and product changes.
- Grow into quantitative optimization work, including improving how we model and select what offers and experiences we serve to each user session.
 Basic Qualifications 
- 3 to 5 years of experience in analytics, analytics engineering, or data science.
- Hands-on experience building with LLMs against real data, including how you validated whether the output was trustworthy. Demos and prompt experimentation are not sufficient.

 WorldStrides is a leading educational travel organization, taking students on learning journeys around the world.  About the problem space 
 AI has changed what's possible in go-to-market, support, and business operations. The constraint is no longer "can we build it" — it's "can we deploy it into a real workflow, prove it made things better, and keep it working."
 Most companies are stuck at the demo stage: a lot of clever prompting, very little that runs reliably on Tuesday morning without someone watching it. This role exists to get us past that, everywhere outside of engineering.

We’re on a mission to empower animal healthcare professionals with opportunities to earn more and achieve greater flexibility in their careers and personal lives.
Powered by groundbreaking technology, Roo has built the industry-leading veterinary staffing platform, connecting Veterinarians, Technicians, and Assistants with animal hospitals for relief work and hiring opportunities. Roo empowers the largest network of over 20,000 veterinary professionals to help more than 9,000 animal hospitals provide quality care to more pets.
Together, we’ve provided more than  3 million hours of healthcare, helping Veterinarians earn more than $200 million.
 About Roo
 Roo is building the modern labor marketplace and operating system for veterinary care. We help hospitals reliably access great veterinary professionals and help veterinary professionals find flexible, meaningful work.
 We're looking for a Revenue Operations Analyst to build the systems and reporting behind Relief-to-Hire, the Roo business that helps hospitals hire the veterinarians and technicians they met through relief shifts. You are accountable for one outcome: a placement pipeline the team trusts, that runs without manual chasing.
 This is not a reporting-only role. Today much of the placement process runs through messages and spreadsheets. You will move it into a real pipeline with clear stages, automated handoffs and numbers everyone uses, so our Career Pathways managers spend their time closing placements instead of tracking them.
 What You'll Own
 Pipeline and CRM
- Build and own the Relief-to-Hire pipeline in our CRM, with stages that match the funnel: relief match, interest from one side, interest from both sides, closed placement.
- Set data standards so every deal has an owner, a stage and a next step.
- Keep one deal per hospital-provider pair, linked to both records, so revenue can be traced to its source.
- Retire manual tracking as the CRM takes over.
 Reporting and Forecasting
- Build the weekly Relief-to-Hire scorecard and placement forecast.
- Find where deals stall and size what fixing each step is worth.
- Make sure placement revenue is attributed correctly across the business units that share it.
 Invoicing and Automation
- Act as the business owner for automated placement invoicing, working with Platform and Finance.
- Write requirements for lifecycle and workflow automations, and measure whether each one worked.
 Experiments and Expansion
- Set up and read tests on fees, terms and outreach, with the holdout defined before launch.
- Extend the same pipeline and reporting to Canada when the business launches there as Locum-to-Hire.
 What Success Looks Like
 In your first year, you will:
- Deliver one trusted Relief-to-Hire scorecard used in the weekly business review.
- Get every active placement deal tracked in the CRM, not in chat or spreadsheets.
- Help launch automated placement invoicing in the US, then Canada.
- Measurably reduce the time Career Pathways managers spend on manual updates.
 What We're Looking For
- Experience in revenue operations, sales operations or business analytics at a marketplace, staffing, recruiting or SaaS company.
- Strong SQL and spreadsheet skills, and experience with a BI tool.
- Hands-on CRM administration experience, such as HubSpot or Salesforce.
- You turn a messy process into clear requirements that engineers and operators can act on.
- A record of changing a team's workflow with them, not to them.
- You understand why different deal types, such as veterinarian and technician placements, need different processes.

- Excellence - We take pride in our craft and expect excellent outcomes in everything we do. We set high standards, verify our work, and own the result. We make deliberate tradeoffs, including rethinking an approach, redoing work, or investing more time.

We distinguish what is necessary from what is familiar and question assumptions that limit possible solutions. We test our reasoning against reality and address root causes with approaches that scale without unnecessary complexity.

We provide an award-winning cloud platform that helps tens of thousands of accounting professionals work more efficiently and collaboratively every day. With customers in 40 countries, we have grown into a globally distributed team across the US, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the Philippines. We are well-funded, ranked #1 on G2, growing rapidly, and have a people-first culture that is recognized with Great Place To Work® certification and on Fortune magazine's Best Small Workplaces™ List.
 Karbon is further ahead on AI adoption than most companies our size. Every department is running AI daily. Hundreds of skills and workflows have been built by our own team. Fourteen department champions drive adoption and share knowledge across the business. The foundation is real and it works.
 The next phase is scale. We need one person whose entire job is extending what we have built, measuring what it returns, and adding the next layer of capability. Not a strategy deck. A working system, the governance that makes it trustworthy, and the numbers that prove it.
 You will report into the CEO and work across every department. You will have the access and sponsorship to make changes stick.
 About the Role 
 Build the Tooling
- Ship internal automations and agents that remove repeated manual work across Sales, CS, Implementation, Support, and Operations. Connect AI to the systems we already run, through APIs and MCP servers.
- The first build is the data gateway. Karbon runs its own MCP server. You extend it into a routing proxy that sits between Claude and every internal data source teams need. Authentication via Okta. RBAC enforcement by department. Request logging for spend attribution and audit. Once the gateway is approved by Security, new connectors plug into a config entry instead of triggering a full review each time. That is your first thirty days.
- After that: CS gets a renewal risk signal. Sales gets a proposal draft automation. Implementation gets a SOW generator with scope-creep flags. Support gets a ticket triage router.
- Prototype fast. Harden what people use. Delete what they ignore. Hand every tool to an owner in the team that uses it. You build it. They run it.

  AvePoint is seeking a highly analytical Data Analyst to support and scale our global partner business. In this role, you will analyze data across our partner ecosystem—including sales performance, customer usage, licensing, and marketing—to provide insights into how our partners drive revenue growth, customer adoption, and long-term retention. Your work will help leadership make decisions on where to invest, which partners to prioritize, and how to grow our channel business effectively.

- Partner Performance Analysis  
 Analyze how partners contribute to revenue growth, pipeline creation, and customer expansion across regions, channels, and segments.

 Develop lifecycle metrics and scorecards to assess partner effectiveness based on engagement, product adoption, customer satisfaction, and training participation.

 Partner with Sales/Go-To-Market, Partner Programs, Marketing, RevOps, and Finance to align on metrics, reporting, and business priorities.

- Experience:  3+ years of experience in data analysis, preferably in a SaaS or technology environment, with a focus on customer data analytics. Experience in SaaS B2B performance metrics such as Annual Recurring Revenue, Net Recurring Revenue, and Gross Recurring Revenue analysis is a plus.   
- Technical Skills:  Proficiency in SQL, Python/R, and data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) a must. - Attention to Detail:  High level of accuracy and attention to detail in data handling and analysis.   
- Business Acumen:  Understanding of sales, marketing, and customer success processes and how data can inform strategy and decision-making.

 About At-Bay  
 At-Bay is the world’s first InsurSec provider designed from the ground up to help businesses tackle cyber risk head on. By combining industry-leading insurance with world-class cybersecurity technology, At-Bay offers end-to-end prevention and protection for the digital age. With 98% of cyber insurance claims in the past five years coming from small and mid-size businesses with revenue under $2B, providing an integrated solution to help manage risk is more critical than ever.
 At-Bay helps its 35,000+ customers close their security technology and skills gap — all through their cyber insurance policy — making them less likely to be hit with a ransomware attack. As a full-stack insurance company, At-Bay offers multiple lines of specialty insurance, including Cyber, Tech E&O, and Miscellaneous Professional Liability (MPL) policies.
 Why you should join our Actuarial Pricing team: 
 As an Senior Actuarial Analyst on the Pricing team, you will be working under the risk function with talented team members in modeling, risk analytics, decision engine, insurance and tech product. The Pricing team has helped At-Bay launch new products, secure reinsurance capacity, quantify and manage risk related KPIs and adjust pricing to drive profitable growth. 
 You’ll join a growing team of actuaries and actuarial analysts of diverse backgrounds and report to our Actuarial Director. You’ll be surrounded by a team that loves what they do, leverages technology to improve efficiency & minimize duplicative work, and recognizes the enormous responsibility that they have – to support key business decisions with data backed insights and a deep understanding of insurance risk. 
 Role overview: 
 Your work will directly contribute to At-Bay’s risk assessment framework that helps with data-driven decisions involving millions of dollars of exposure. This is a multidisciplinary role that includes developing deep cyber and tech knowledge, business acumen, research, and analytical skills. This is also a hands-on operational role where you’ll see in house submission, quotes and binds and understand how each risk decision will impact on the business.
 You will manage the overall program profitability, improve pricing accuracy, and work cross-functionally with Insurance & Tech Product, Underwriting, Claims, and Decision Engine teams on the implementation of those products. You will be responsible for leading and supporting a wide variety of pricing and underwriting related initiatives, quantifying the impacts and implications of those initiatives on the business and identifying ways to the overall economics of the business.
 How you’ll make an impact:  
 By 3 months…
- You’ll understand At-Bay’s internal data structure and develop key relationships across the business
- You’ll have reviewed the existing Cyber and Tech E&O product structures, related tools, and related data sources to track and analyze product performance
- You’ll have completed a quarterly rate indication and presented your recommendation to key stakeholders
- You’ll identify areas of improvement in our systems and processes 
 By 6 months...
- You’ll have developed a proposal to modify the Cyber rate plan and have evaluated the proposal will have on the business
- You’ll have improved the depth and efficiency of the existing rate indication process via automation and/or innovation
- You’ll have analyzed customer acquisition and retention data to improve At-Bay’s ability to understand the economics of the business
- You’ll help coach team members and key to understand actuarial analytics, Cyber pricing and risk, and how it differs from traditional pricing and other lines of business

- You’ve evaluated the profitability of a portfolio of insureds using actuarial techniques and communicated the results to leadership
