Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the country in which the role is being hired. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.
 Mark43's mission is to empower communities and their governments with new technologies that improve the safety and quality of life for all. We build powerful, scalable, and elegant software that sets a new standard for the tools upon which our first responders rely. Our users are diverse, and we are committed to embracing diversity of thought and experience within our team.   
 We are looking for a  Manager of Revenue Accounting to join our Finance & Accounting team as an individual contributor. This role sits at the center of our quote-to-cash architecture and serves as the financial owner of the revenue across our operational systems. You will combine deep technical accounting expertise with strong business systems judgment to ensure complex SaaS and Professional Services arrangements are structured, allocated, billed, and recognized accurately at scale.   
 Role Summary   
 This role will oversee the revenue recognition process across SaaS and Professional Services, ensuring the data flowing from Salesforce to NetSuite is complete, accurate, and audit ready. You will be the person who can interpret ASC 606 and work across Mark43’s stakeholders, including Revenue Operations, Deals Desk, Professional Services, and FP&A.   
 The ideal candidate has a rare blend of technical revenue and financial systems expertise. You are equally comfortable writing a revenue memo, reviewing SSP methodology, applying fair value allocation concepts, driving system automations and process improvements, forecasting revenue and collections, and providing tactical advice to Revenue Operations and Deals Desk on the financial and systems impact of upstream changes to the sales process.   
 What  You’ll  Do   
 Technical Accounting   
- Own the technical revenue accounting framework for multi-element customer arrangements, with deep application of  ASC 606 across SaaS , Professional Services, renewals, expansions, modifications, credits, and bundled deals.    
- Determine performance obligations and ensure contracts are evaluated appropriately for distinct goods and services, timing of recognition, and allocation across arrangements.    
- Lead the company’s approach to  Standalone Selling Price (SSP)  and allocation methodologies, including relative fair value allocation concepts used in practice to support consistent and defensible revenue treatment.

- Take Ownership: We own outcomes, not just our individual work. We make decisions that move the company forward and follow through.

- Build Great Teams: We lead by example, empower others, and create healthy teams where people can do their best work.

 What We're Looking For

You'll own compensation philosophy, incentive and equity design, and the models and tools the business actually runs on: market research turned into clear recommendations, offer and leveling frameworks that People and Finance reach for, and fast, defensible answers in the moments that matter: performance cycles, offer decisions, retention calls.

- Own the cycles. Run annual and off-cycle comp planning end to end: strategy, budget, execution. Stay hands-on through the last approval.

ABOUT OLIPOP 
 At OLIPOP, we’re on a mission to positively impact consumer health at scale. And we’re doing it through something simple: soda. But not just any soda, a new kind of soda: one that’s delicious, refreshing, and actually good for you.
 This mission is deeply personal for our CEO, Co-Founder, and Formulator, Ben Goodwin. Like many of us, Ben grew up consuming the Standard American Diet: lots of soda and processed foods that prioritized convenience over nutrition. But at 14, he took his health into his own hands. After making significant changes to his nutrition and exercise, he lost 50 pounds and saw a transformation in his energy, mood, and emotional clarity.
 Those changes sparked a deep curiosity about the connection between nutrition and health. Ben became a relentless student of the gut microbiome and the ways it supports overall wellness. The more he discovered, the more passionate he became about finding credible, science-backed ways to make consumer health accessible to everyone.
 The mission was clear. The vehicle? Less so. After exploring the possibilities, Ben landed on an unexpected yet familiar choice: soda. It was something he loved as a kid, and he knew millions shared that same nostalgia. But this wouldn’t be just any soda. With most Americans falling short on daily fiber, Ben set out to create a version with more fiber and less sugar, one that was perfectly balanced. The result? A deliciously refreshing soda with 6 to 9 grams of fiber and 2 to 5 grams of sugar, delivering science-backed benefits without sacrificing the classic taste people crave.
 In 2018, the first OLIPOP cans hit the shelves, bringing Ben’s vision to life with a functional soda that anyone could enjoy. And by reimagining soda, we’re also reshaping culture. That means creating products that support health for all and building a business grounded in humanistic values: empathy, integrity, and a belief in better for everyone. From the ingredients we source to the culture we foster, we’re committed to proving that business (and beverage!) can be a force for good, and that soda has the power to bring people together.
 So join us, and let’s write a new American soda story together. One we can all feel good about. One OLIPOP at a time.

They’ll partner closely with internal teams and external research vendors, serving as a trusted advisor on insight-led decisions that drive both short-term performance and long-term brand growth. This role is a great fit for someone with deep functional expertise who’s curious, collaborative, and passionate about extending our insights capabilities across the organization.

ABOUT OLIPOP 
 At OLIPOP, we’re on a mission to positively impact consumer health at scale. And we’re doing it through something simple: soda. But not just any soda, a new kind of soda: one that’s delicious, refreshing, and actually good for you.
 This mission is deeply personal for our CEO, Co-Founder, and Formulator, Ben Goodwin. Like many of us, Ben grew up consuming the Standard American Diet: lots of soda and processed foods that prioritized convenience over nutrition. But at 14, he took his health into his own hands. After making significant changes to his nutrition and exercise, he lost 50 pounds and saw a transformation in his energy, mood, and emotional clarity.
 Those changes sparked a deep curiosity about the connection between nutrition and health. Ben became a relentless student of the gut microbiome and the ways it supports overall wellness. The more he discovered, the more passionate he became about finding credible, science-backed ways to make consumer health accessible to everyone.
 The mission was clear. The vehicle? Less so. After exploring the possibilities, Ben landed on an unexpected yet familiar choice: soda. It was something he loved as a kid, and he knew millions shared that same nostalgia. But this wouldn’t be just any soda. With most Americans falling short on daily fiber, Ben set out to create a version with more fiber and less sugar, one that was perfectly balanced. The result? A deliciously refreshing soda with 6 to 9 grams of fiber and 2 to 5 grams of sugar, delivering science-backed benefits without sacrificing the classic taste people crave.
 In 2018, the first OLIPOP cans hit the shelves, bringing Ben’s vision to life with a functional soda that anyone could enjoy. And by reimagining soda, we’re also reshaping culture. That means creating products that support health for all and building a business grounded in humanistic values: empathy, integrity, and a belief in better for everyone. From the ingredients we source to the culture we foster, we’re committed to proving that business (and beverage!) can be a force for good, and that soda has the power to bring people together.
 So join us, and let’s write a new American soda story together. One we can all feel good about. One OLIPOP at a time.

About Blank Street 
 At Blank Street, we’re on a mission to become the defining food and beverage brand of our generation. From the very beginning, we’ve set out to add a spark to ordinary experiences through elevated products, attention-to-detail, and a commitment to making every moment memorable. We’re motivated by the millions of customers we serve across cities, and know that our potential is unlimited. It all starts with our people and their commitment to make magic happen each and every day.
 Like the sound of this? Keep reading.
 Start Something Extraordinary…  
 As an Operations Manager at Blank Street, you are the ultimate leader of an entire area of 5+ stores and the General Managers who lead them.
 That means your greatest responsibility is growing people. You will hire, coach and develop an A* team of GMs, helping them become confident leaders who build engaged, high-performing teams across our stores.
You are also the strategic mind behind your stores: you will own your area's PnL and decide how to plan, prioritize and follow through, so your stores get better day by day. In a fast-moving and constantly evolving business, you will create clarity, build capability, and foster a culture of accountability, hospitality and continuous improvement.
 You'll report to the Director of Operations and work closely with the rest of our Field Leadership team. Together, you'll help scale the next generation of leaders while driving an exceptional experience for both our teams and our customers.
 What You'll Own
 Be Our Ultimate Hospitality Leader 
- Make the standards stick: Coach your GMs to build the systems, behaviors and processes that keep our hospitality standards high every shift, whether you're in the store or not.
- Hold the bar: Check standards across your area through regular store visits and data, and hold GMs accountable for closing gaps fast.
- Jump in where it counts: Take an active role in turning around struggling stores and launching new stores in your area.
 Run a Tight PnL 
- Plan for demand: Take quarterly sales forecasts from HQ, translate them store by store and make sure every GM knows what's coming (growth, slowdowns, seasonality, new openings nearby).
- Build the labor plan: Set labor targets a quarter out, including headcount and transfers between stores, and coach GMs to build rotas against them.
- Calibrate inventory: Help GMs calibrate inventory to forecast demand, and set clear guardrails so no store is badly overstocked or running short.
 Build and Develop an A-Team 
- Develop your GMs: Grow GMs into future leaders through our training pathways, regular 1:1s and direct feedback.
- Own the talent pipeline: Calibrate hiring and promotion decisions across your area and set quarterly succession targets from barista to GM, so every store has its next leader ready.
- Build an area-wide culture: Turn your stores into one team that shares what works and backs each other, with a culture that's distinctly Blank Street: fast-moving, high-energy, collaborative and fun.
 Operate Strategically 
- Know your numbers inside out: Master your stores' KPIs and PnL, and set clear priorities for your area every week and every quarter.
- Make sure every store has a plan: Work with each GM to build a plan for their store, then stay close as they carry it out and push the numbers in the right direction.
- Land change and innovation: Roll out new initiatives across your area, from menu launches to tech tools. That means clear comms, hands-on training and real buy-in from your teams, then tracking adoption until it sticks.
 Who We’re Looking For 
- 5+ years of leadership experience in hospitality, retail, or another fast-growing consumer business.
- Experience leading multiple locations (3-10) and developing the managers who run them.
- Passionate about hospitality: you love creating exceptional customer and employee experiences, and care about setting the bar high in every store you’ve managed.

About the Job: 
 LaunchDarkly is seeking a People Systems, Analytics and AI Manager to be our subject matter expert on HR systems and to turn People data into insights that help business leaders make better decisions. You will build the reports, analytics, and dashboards that tell the story of our workforce, and you will use AI tooling to make those stories faster to create, easier to understand, and more compelling.
 This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Director, People Programs, Systems and Analytics. You will work closely with People Operations, Finance, and leaders across the business, and you will own your work from question to insight to action. 
 We are looking for someone who combines deep HR systems knowledge with strong analytical skills, creativity in how data is presented, and sound judgment about people data and AI.
 Responsibilities:
- Serve as the subject matter expert for our HR systems (HRIS, applicant tracking, performance, compensation, and learning platforms), including configuration, data integrity, security roles, integrations, and release management.
- Design, build, and maintain reports, dashboards, and analytics on headcount, hiring, retention, engagement, compensation, and workforce planning that leaders use to make decisions.
- Partner with People, Finance, and business leaders to translate questions into clear metrics, definitions, and analyses, and to recommend actions based on what the data shows.
- Use AI tools to accelerate analysis and create compelling data stories and visualizations, including automated insights, natural-language summaries, and executive-ready narratives.
- Establish and govern People data standards: metric definitions, data quality checks, documentation, and a single source of truth across systems.
- Protect employee data by applying privacy, confidentiality, and access controls, and by partnering with Legal and Security on responsible use of AI with People data.
- Own the intake, prioritization, and delivery of system and reporting requests, balancing quick turnarounds with scalable, self-service solutions.
- Automate recurring reports and manual workflows to reduce effort and errors, and identify new opportunities where systems and AI can improve the employee and manager experience.
- Support system projects such as new module rollouts, integrations, data migrations, and annual cycles (performance, compensation, and engagement), including testing, training, and documentation.
- Enable People Operations teammates and managers through training, office hours, and clear guides so they can use data and tools with confidence.
- Stay current on HR technology, analytics, and AI trends, and bring practical recommendations to the Director, People Programs, Systems and Analytics.
 Qualifications:
- 8+ years of related experience in HR systems, People analytics, or HR operations, with hands-on ownership of reporting and dashboards in a technology or high-growth environment.
- Expert-level knowledge of at least one major HRIS (for example, Workday, Rippling, or similar), including report writing, calculated fields, and security configuration.
- Strong proficiency with analytics and visualization tools (for example, SQL, Tableau, Looker, Power BI, or similar) and advanced spreadsheet skills.
- Demonstrated fluency with AI tooling to analyze data, generate insights, and build visualizations and narratives, with sound judgment about accuracy and appropriate use.
- Ability to translate business questions into metrics and communicate findings clearly to non-technical leaders.
- Strong understanding of data integrity, privacy, and confidentiality practices for employee data.
- Proven ability to manage multiple projects and stakeholders independently and deliver on time with attention to detail.
- Curious, pragmatic problem solver who enjoys simplifying complex processes and data.
- Comfortable working with a highly distributed team across time zone

About SecurityScorecard: 
 SecurityScorecard is the global leader in cybersecurity ratings, with over 12 million companies continuously rated, operating in 64 countries. Founded in 2013 by security and risk experts Dr. Alex Yampolskiy and Sam Kassoumeh and funded by world-class investors, SecurityScorecard’s patented rating technology is used by over 25,000 organizations for self-monitoring, third-party risk management, board reporting, and cyber insurance underwriting; making all organizations more resilient by allowing them to easily find and fix cybersecurity risks across their digital footprint.  
 Headquartered in New York City, our culture has been recognized by Inc Magazine as a "Best Workplace,” by Crain’s NY as a "Best Places to Work in NYC," and as one of the 10 hottest SaaS startups in New York for two years in a row. Most recently, SecurityScorecard was named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies for 2023 and to the Achievers 50 Most Engaged Workplaces in 2023 award recognizing “forward-thinking employers for their unwavering commitment to employee engagement.”  SecurityScorecard is proud to be funded by world-class investors including Silver Lake Waterman, Moody’s, Sequoia Capital, GV and Riverwood Capital. 
 About the Role: 
 SecurityScorecard's Product & Design org is rebuilding itself around AI-first workflows, where designers prototype directly against the live codebase with Claude and hand off working interactions instead of static Figma comps, and where AI agents increasingly operate alongside human users inside our product. We need an operator to build and run the systems that make both sides of that work: the human design org, and the emerging discipline of agent experience (AX).
 This is a design/UX operations and program management role, not a design-execution role. You won't be shipping mockups. You'll be building the operating model, cadence, metrics, and standards that let a pod-based, AI-first org move fast and stay aligned, on the human experience side and on the agent experience side alike.
 This role follows a hybrid work model based on proximity to our office locations. Employees who live within 75 miles of our Midtown NYC or Downtown Austin office are required to work onsite 1–2 days per week. Employees who live outside a 75-mile radius of both offices are eligible for fully remote work.
 What You'll Do 
- Design and run the operating model for a pod-based design org: designers embedded in cross-functional product pods, owning continuity per product area, no central ticket queue.
- Drive adoption of AI-first design practices: designers prototyping from the live codebase and design system with Claude (or equivalent), shipping working interaction detail instead of static comps.
- Own design-to-engineering handoff so interaction details, the details that get lost between Figma and code, are captured, accurate, and buildable on arrival.
- Own agent experience (AX) operations: coordinate the evals, guardrails, and agent primitives (permissions, tool access, escalation paths, failure handling) that let agents operate reliably and safely across the product.
- Define how humans and agents hand off to each other, and how multiple agents coordinate with each other, so collaboration is designed on purpose rather than emerging by accident.
- Define and track the metrics that prove the org is moving faster and improving the overall experience: prototyping velocity, handoff quality, cycle time, agent eval coverage, and AI-tooling adoption on both the human and agent sides.
- Run planning, prioritization, and cross-pod cadence, including shared or infrastructure-level design work that spans product lines.
- Support customer co-build and live-prototyping sessions, making sure what's learned scales across similar customers instead of staying one-off.
- Partner with the UX Director and pod leads to onboard designers into the AI-first workflow and raise the bar on t

About Pursuit
 Pursuit is a social impact organization building the future of economic mobility in the age of AI. For over a decade, we've transformed lives through immersive training programs that propel adults from low-income backgrounds — often without college degrees — into high-growth tech careers. Our graduates, who we call Builders, have generated nearly $1 billion in lifetime wage gains.
 As AI reshapes every industry, Pursuit is becoming an AI-native organization — training AI-native talent, embedding AI into our operations, and building scalable systems to extend our impact. From local partnerships to national policy, we're rethinking how opportunity works at scale.
 The Role
 Pursuit is hiring a Senior Manager, Strategic Partnerships to join our External Affairs team at a pivotal moment of growth.
 This role sits at the intersection of government and education/workforce partnerships, policy, and execution. You will be the day-to-day operating lead for a multi-year, state-funded initiative that brings Pursuit’s AI-native training to three New York regions in partnership with community colleges, workforce nonprofits, and regional economic development organizations. You'll take it from contract award through partner mobilization to launch, and then help us turn what we learn into a model other markets can run.
 The ideal candidate is a strong operator and relationship-builder who thrives in complex, multi-stakeholder environments, brings rigor to systems and processes, and understands how partnerships power mission-driven scale. You are comfortable being the person who holds the timeline when multiple organizations each own a piece of it.
 What You'll Do
 Partner Management & Delivery
- Serve as the day-to-day owner of a portfolio of workforce, higher education, employer, and economic development partners
- Run the partnership operating rhythm: recurring check-ins, all-partner convenings, and a shared view of status, owners, and next steps that every party trusts
- Shepherd agreements from term sheet to execution in partnership with cross-functional internal stakeholders
- Negotiate and hold the line on deliverables, timelines, and shared definitions: who recruits, who teaches, who reports, what counts as success
- Surface partner risk early and drive it to resolution rather than reporting it
- Onboard new partners and build the templates, briefing materials, and playbooks that make the next partnership faster to stand up
 Grant & Contract Stewardship
- Manage public grants and contracts from post-award through closeout: workplans, milestones, reporting calendars, and modifications
- Own reporting, compliance, documentation, and audit readiness, including subrecipient monitoring and pass-through requirements
- Serve as the primary operational point of contact for government partners 
- Partner with Finance on budgets, invoicing, reimbursement mechanics, disbursement schedules, and partner payments
 Cross-Functional Execution
- Translate external commitments into internal project plans with defined scope, timelines, named owners, and deliverables — and hold the org to them
- Run the internal cadence that keeps delivery on track: workstream check-ins, milestone or gate reviews, and a single source of truth for status
- Partner with Program and Instruction on staffing, curriculum adaptation, train-the-trainer, and cohort calendars; with Admissions and Recruitment on candidate profiles and enrollment targets; with Finance on contracting and subawards
- Broker decisions that cross team lines, escalating clearly, with options and a recommendation, rather than letting them sit
- Drive internal knowledge sharing and continuous improvement based on partner insights, project learnings, and ecosystem trends
- Use AI tools daily to compress the operational overhead of this work — tracking, drafting, synthesis, reporting — and share what works with the team
 Ecosystem & Representation
- Represent Pursuit

We're committed to providing innovative and accessible financial solutions, and data plays a crucial role in driving our success. We're looking for a talented and passionate Data Analyst to join our Payments team and help us leverage data to optimize our operations, enhance our products, and deliver exceptional customer experiences.
 ABOUT THE ROLE 
 As a Data Analyst on the Payments team, you'll be at the forefront of shaping our understanding of customer behavior, payments product performance, and operational efficiency. You'll work closely with product managers, engineers, and other stakeholders to translate business questions into actionable insights. Your work will directly impact key decisions related to our banking products, features, and overall strategy.

- Analyze large datasets to uncover trends, patterns, and improvement opportunities in banking products and services.
- Build and maintain dashboards and reports to track KPIs and deliver clear insights to stakeholders.

- Partner with product managers and engineers to define and measure the success of features and initiatives.

- Monitor and analyze customer behavior across deposits, transactions, and other banking activities.
- Deliver actionable insights to leadership on emerging trends and innovation opportunities.

- Communicate findings and recommendations effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Continuously improve data analysis processes and methodologies.
- Uphold data integrity, accuracy, and governance across analytics pipelines.
- Support production analytics and fraud response through participation in on-call rotations.
 REQUIREMENTS 
- Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or a related field.
- Experience as a data analyst for 3+ years, ideally in B2C, financial services, or technology.
- Strong proficiency in SQL and experience working with relational databases (e.g., Bigquery, Snowflake, Redshift, etc).
- Proficient in utilizing data visualization tools like Tableau, Looker, or other similar platforms.
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with a strong attention to detail.
- Ability to communicate complex data insights clearly and effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Strong business acumen and the ability to translate business questions into data analysis plans.
- Experience with A/B testing and experimental design.
- Working experience with Python for data analysis.
 ADDITIONAL DESIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS 
- Familiarity with the fintech industry and banking products is a plus.
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
- Exposure to dimensional modeling concepts to power meaningful analytics.
- Experience building data pipelines in dbt.
- Familiarity with machine learning techniques and predictive analytics is a plus.
- Experience modeling data using dbt.

- Discretionary performance bonus program 
- Biannual performance reviews

About us: 
 Kiva is a global nonprofit, founded in 2005, with a mission to expand financial access and help underserved communities thrive. Kiva unlocks capital for borrowers through crowdfunded loans supported by individuals around the world. Lenders on Kiva can start with as little as $25 to support causes that matter most to them, whether that’s gender equity and support for women, refugees, climate change, small businesses, agriculture, and more. Since our founding, over two million people have invested  over $2 billion  in real dreams and real opportunity, spanning more than  100 countries  and  over 5 million  borrowers
 As we work toward our mission, Kiva invests in building and retaining a global team of talent to add to our values-driven and digital-first culture. Our organization is supported by over 700 volunteers and 130+ full time employees dispersed around the world, as well as within team hubs located in San Francisco, Nairobi, Bogota, and Bangkok. Kiva’s team is growing as we pursue exciting new opportunities to scale our impact and create a financially inclusive world.
 Kiva's values: 
 Impact first - This is why we exist. This is the drumbeat we march to. Every day.
 Extreme ownership - Own it; you, your relationships, your impact. Insist that others support you and hold you accountable.
 Be curious and bold - Never stop learning. Question assumptions. Take Risks and dream big.
 Inclusion. Equity. Diversity. - Without reservation and without caveat. In our hiring, in our workplace and in our impact in the world.
 Honor and integrity - Do the most right thing in the most right way. Cherish diversity and respect each other.
 Love and kindness always - Say what you mean. Mean what you say. And don't say it mean. Clarity. Courage. Kindness.
 Role overview: 
 The Manager, Strategic Partnerships helps grow philanthropic support for Kiva by cultivating individual donors, engaging philanthropic advisors and donor-advised fund partners, and developing compelling donor communications. This role manages a portfolio of mid-level donors and prospects, builds pathways to major giving, and translates Kiva’s impact into opportunities for deeper engagement and support.
 As an individual contributor on the Strategic Partnerships team, you will work closely with colleagues across Finance, Marketing and Communications, Product and Engineering, and impact-focused teams to strengthen donor relationships, improve the giving experience, and support proposals and reporting. Success requires sound judgment, strong writing, and the ability to independently manage complex work while collaborating across teams.
 At this time, we can only consider applicants with authorization to work in the United States on a permanent, full-time basis; unfortunately we cannot provide visa sponsorship. 
 Key responsibilities include:  
- Individual and mid-level donor strategy and engagement (40%) 
- Manage and cultivate relationships with a portfolio composed primarily of mid-level and major-tier donors and prospects, with support from Strategic Partnerships colleagues. Develop tailored engagement, solicitation, and stewardship plans that deepen commitment and create pathways to major gifts.
- Develop and implement an engagement strategy for donor-advised fund sponsors, philanthropic advisors, and other “gatekeeper” professionals who influence charitable giving. Equip Kiva relationship managers with approaches and resources they can use to build these partnerships.
- Partner with colleagues to improve website journeys, digital communications, and unique Kiva offerings such as managed lending for mid-level and major donors.
- Represent Kiva in donor and advisor conversations, bringing in colleagues with relevant expertise when needed. Pursue thought leadership opportunities through articles, conference presentations, and other relevant channels.
- Plan and deliver in-person and virtual donor events with the Strategic Partnerships team

You'll build, validate, and maintain actuarial and CAT models that tell us what property insurance should cost for our clients, and you'll turn that output into recommendations our brokers can use with risk managers and CFOs.  • Turn model output into something a client can read. Think slides, benchmarks, and short written narratives our brokers can put in front of a CFO without translating. 
 • Sit with producers, property practice leaders, and clients to walk through the numbers, take the hard questions, and help shape program structure.

About the job 
 Do you thrive on building people functions from the ground up, love partnering directly with leadership to shape culture and talent strategy, and get energized by fast-paced, scaling environments? 
 Join Artefact, a global data and AI consulting firm helping organizations turn data into business impact. With 2,000+ employees across 34 offices worldwide, we partner with world-class clients such as Samsung, L'Oréal, and LVMH to accelerate digital transformation through data and AI. 
 Founded in Paris, Artefact has grown from a small team into a global organization — and our people strategy has had to scale right alongside it. As we enter our next phase of growth in the US and Canada, we're looking for a Sr. HRBP ready to help build the systems, culture, and talent foundation that will support that growth. 
 Find out more at artefact.com . 
 The Opportunity 
 As Sr. HRBP you will lead several areas central to Artefact’s continued growth: employee relations, manager advisory, talent development, onboarding, and employee experience. You will also oversee benefits administration and the execution of immigration and global mobility programs across North America. 
 Reporting to the Head of People, you will have the autonomy to shape these programs and translate People strategy into practical, scalable experiences for employees and managers. You will work directly with business leaders, Chapter Leads, employees, the Resource Manager, and global People partners to strengthen how Artefact supports, develops, and retains its people. 
 This role is designed for someone who enjoys building, solving complex people challenges, advising managers, and staying close to the employee experience. You will have broad visibility, meaningful access to leadership, and the opportunity to influence how Artefact’s North American People practices evolve as the business grows. 
 What You’ll Own 
 Employee Relations and Manager Advisory 
- Serve as the primary day-to-day People advisor to employees and managers across the United States and Canada. 
- Manage employee relations matters, including investigations, conflict resolution, performance concerns, accommodations, and workplace issues. 
- Coach managers through feedback, difficult conversations, employee concerns, and employment decisions with empathy, consistency, and sound judgment. 
- Develop practical guidance that helps managers navigate employee matters confidently and consistently. 
- Identify recurring employee and manager concerns and recommend appropriate policy, process, training, or organizational improvements. 
- Partner with the Head of People and employment counsel on sensitive, complex, or high-risk matters. 
- Support the consistent implementation and application of North American People policies. 
 Talent Development 
- Lead manager coaching and enablement, including feedback, development conversations, team effectiveness, and difficult performance discussions. 
- Design and deliver manager, leadership, and professional-development initiatives aligned with organizational needs. 
- Own performance-related employee relations matters, including performance concerns, documentation, performance-improvement plans, corrective action, and manager guidance. 
- Partner with the Resource Manager on talent reviews, individual development plans, and organization-wide capability gaps, bringing manager and employee-relations insights alongside performance, skills, staffing, and career-development data. 
- Partner with the Resource Manager and Chapter Leads to translate identified capability gaps into appropriate technical, professional, manager, and leadership-development initiatives. 
- Translate employee-relations, manager, and talent insights into recommendations for development, policy, and organizational improvement. 
- Step in to support Talent Acquisition during high-volume hiring periods, as needed.

(NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion. 
 Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.
 About The Job 
 OpenTable is looking for an Associate Manager, Accounting to own a highly technical portfolio spanning partnership revenue, loyalty, and leases, along with other technical areas such as bad debt, prepaids, and accruals, and the close-related operations that support them. The role sits at the intersection of technical accounting, revenue recognition, contract interpretation, and cross-functional business partnership.
 This is an Associate Manager–level individual contributor role with significant ownership and influence: you'll lead complex workstreams, coach teammates, streamline processes, and work cross-functionally to support business partners. It's built for someone with strong judgment and technical depth who can navigate the organization independently, lead day-to-day execution, communicate plan and progress clearly, and improve how the work gets done. This role reports to the Manager, Accounting. This posting is for an existing vacancy.
 Responsibilities 
- Own the end-to-end accounting for fast-growing strategic partnership revenue programs, managing complex models to support revenue and expense recognition and balance sheet treatment
- Own the technical accounting for the evolving loyalty program, using judgment to evaluate the key assumptions that drive it
- Lead the accounting across other technical areas including leases, bad debt, prepaids, and accruals, spanning multiple OpenTable legal entities, all reported under US GAAP
- Manage close-related accounting activities, including journal entries, reconciliations, and balance sheet integrity across these areas
- Organize and lead cross-functional workstreams, building strong, productive working relationships with stakeholders across the company — including teammates and partners in Finance, Product, Legal, Sales, Strategy, Operations, and AP
- Prepare clear technical accounting memos and documentation, support internal controls, and walk internal and external auditors through positions and supporting evidence
- Drive process improvements that reduce manual work and help the team scale, through stronger process design, system connectivity, and AI-enabled workflows
 Minimum Qualifications 
- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
- 6+ years of progressive accounting experience with deep knowledge of US GAAP, including operationalizing guidance for revenue recognition (ASC 606) and lease accounting (ASC 842).
- CPA certification or equivalent technical accounting depth.
- Advanced Excel proficiency, including extensive experience with complex financial modeling, lookups, and pivot tables.
- Demonstrated analytical, communication, and stakeholder-management skills with the ability to collaborate across technical and non-technical teams.
 Preferred Qualifications 
- Experience in public accounting or professional financial services.
- Proficiency with NetSuite or similar enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.
- Demonstrated interest or experience in utilizing artificial intelligence and automation tools to enhance process scalability and quality.
 Benefits and Perks 
- Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year
- Focus on mental health and well-being:
- Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth
- Company-paid subscription to Heads

Addepar unifies portfolio, market and client data in a total portfolio view and delivers AI-powered insights within investment and client workflows. More than 1,500 firms in 60 countries use Addepar to manage and advise on nearly $10 trillion in assets. Its open platform integrates with 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and levels of complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, São Paulo, London, Edinburgh, Geneva, Warsaw, Dubai, Pune and Singapore.
 The Role 
 We are currently seeking a Sr. Manager, Security Operations to lead our Global Security Operations team within Addepar’s Information Security & Risk organization. In this role, you will own the day-to-day running of our detection and response function, act as incident commander for security incidents, and partner with our 24/7 MSSP to ensure threats are identified and handled quickly. You will set the operational objectives and strategy for Security Operations, lead and grow a global team, and shape our detection strategy for threats specific to Addepar’s environment. Beyond the immediate response, you will make sure we learn from every incident by driving post-incident follow-through, turning incident trends into lasting fixes with partners across the business, and reporting on the health of the program to Security leadership. - AI-Driven Modernization: Lead the modernization of our SecOps function through AIOps, using AI and automation to streamline alert triage, enrichment, investigation and response, reduce manual toil, and scale the team’s impact

Sell what you love. For us and millions of users across the globe, that’s Spotify. Join the Sales team and you’ll build the relationships that help grow our business in existing markets and beyond. We don’t just sell creative solutions to our clients and partners, we help to shape them; using our expert knowledge of ad products, sales channels and the industry to impact the way the world experiences music and podcasts. 


Our Revenue Growth team drives advertiser acquisition and retention at scale by turning data into action. We build and run scalable go-to-market programs that help advertisers succeed, through lifecycle communications and seller-facing actions. 
As a Senior Program Analyst - GTM Ops, you'll own the technical layer that makes Revenue Growth actually run. Working within Spotify's broader data infrastructure, you'll build the team-specific tools, endpoints, and pipelines our programs depend on — the reporting that helps sellers act, the data feeds that power our advertiser tools, the pipelines that keep everything moving. Your work won't be abstract; it shows up directly in what the team ships and what sellers experience.


What You’ll Do
- Work on high-impact data problems that support revenue growth and help our advertising business scale
- Build and maintain dbt models and BigQuery pipelines that power team tools and seller-facing reporting
- Monitor pipeline health, identify issues early, and partner with data engineering and Insights teams to resolve upstream challenges
- Create dashboards and reports that sales teams rely on, translating business needs into clear, actionable views
- Partner closely with sales teams and leadership to understand needs, scope solutions, and deliver data that supports prioritization and decision-making
- Improve how data is used in the sales process by surfacing signals that help teams focus, personalize outreach, and close opportunities
- Support and extend pipelines that process unstructured data using LLMs, ensuring outputs are reliable, validated, and usable within BigQuery

Who You Are
- You have 4+ years of experience in analytics engineering, BI engineering, or data/reporting roles, ideally supporting go-to-market, growth, or sales teams
- You are experienced with SQL and BigQuery, and build with reliability and maintainability in mind
- You have worked with dbt and understand how to extend and maintain models within an existing DAG
- You enjoy building systems that work consistently for a team and take pride in operational reliability
- You communicate clearly and can partner directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand needs and deliver solutions
- You are comfortable translating business questions into structured data outputs and reporting
- You are curious about applying AI in data workflows, including working with or learning about LLM-driven pipelines

Where You’ll Be
- This role is based in New York City.
- We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

The United States base range for this position is $92,293 - 131,847, plus equity. These ranges may be modified in the future.

(Hybrid, 3 days onsite) Base: $80,000 - $130,000 + Share Options 
 The Company: 
 Stream is on a mission to bring financial wellbeing to all workers.
 We partner with some of the world's most well-known employers, like Crate & Barrel, Driven Brands, General Electric, New Balance, Restaurant Brands International (RBI) and others, to give their teams access to fairer financial services. Over 3 million people track their shifts and earnings, start their first savings account, use budgeting tools, access financial education and choose when they want to get paid. All in one smartphone app.
 Stream is unique: VC-backed and growing at scale-up pace, but with a social conscience. Some of the world's leading financial charities and impact funds were our founding investors.
 You'd be joining a team of over 300 passionate, ambitious people across the UK, Europe and US, building a category-leading FinTech product with the mission to improve the lives of millions.
 The role 
 You will be the second data person dedicated to the US business, working alongside our Lead Data Engineer in the US and as part of the central Data team. The US has grown significantly and just launched its largest customer to date. That growth creates real demand for analysis: commercial teams want to quantify customer ROI, product wants to understand adoption across multiple US products, and finance, compliance and state regulators need accurate, reproducible reporting. 
 This is an analytics engineering role in the full sense. You model data in dbt, you build the dashboards and data apps people use in StreamBI, and you sit with business stakeholders to turn a vague question into a defined analysis. You own a business area end to end rather than handing work between an analyst and an engineer. 
 What you will work on 
- Customer ROI Program: Partner with our US GTM and implementation teams on the data side of a new client-facing programme: define what data we ask customers for, what the minimum viable extract is, how it lands securely, and then run the repeatable analyses that show clients the impact Stream has on turnover, retention and absenteeism. 
- US commercial and product analytics. Build the adoption, engagement and cohort analysis on top of our per-product usage layer, and give the commercial team a validated set of statistics they can put in front of prospects. 
- Regulatory and financial reporting. Take over execution of our state regulatory reports and examiner follow-ups using the scaffolded pipeline we have built, and extend our financial integrity checks across US salary and settlement data. 
- Dashboards and data apps. Build and maintain US dashboards in StreamBI, our Streamlit-based BI platform, replacing legacy Redash and Sigma reporting. 
- Shared responsibilities. Around a fifth of your time goes to the things every analytics engineer here does: triaging dbt and data quality alerts, answering questions in #ask-data, reviewing PRs across our dbt and StreamBI repos, and keeping documentation current. 
 Within six months you should own the US commercial analytics domain outright, be running state regulatory reports without supervision, and be the first person US stakeholders think to ask. 
 Key technologies 
 SQL, Snowflake, dbt, Python, Streamlit, GitHub, Claude Code 
 What we are looking for 
- Two to four years in analytics engineering, or in a data analyst role where you built and owned the models as well as the outputs. 
- Strong SQL, including the discipline to reconcile numbers and prove they tie out, not just aggregate them. 
- Hands-on dbt experience, and the ability to read and extend a dimensional model without breaking its grain. 
- Python sufficient to build data apps in Streamlit, or a clear track record of picking up a similar framework fast. 
- Experience working directly with commercial or operational stakeholders: taking an ambiguous request, redefining it, and returning something that changed a decision.
